A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MPG-SAM 2 work and contain readable equations, Figures 1–5, Tables 1–8, and Appendices A–B. The material can be matched despite layout shifts and citation renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original RVOS benchmark results, component ablations, model-configuration studies, and qualitative segmentation examples in Section 4 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v5 retains the original benchmark, ablation, and supplementary results in Tables 1–8, together with qualitative segmentation results in Figures 4–5.

M1.justification: The encoder, mask prior generator, global-historical aggregator, decoding procedure, and losses remain unchanged. Figure 2's revised arrows and decoder label match the procedure already described in v3 Section 3.4 and Figure 3; they do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Ref-YouTube-VOS, Ref-DAVIS17, and MeViS evaluation, RefCOCO/+/g pretraining, and the same occlusion, multiple-target, and similar-object scenarios in Appendix B.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–2 and 5–6 and Figure 4, including the same ReferFormer, SgMg, VISA, and HyperSeg comparisons where applicable. The newly cited works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same validation sets, J/F/J&F metrics, preprocessing, training schedules, frame counts, model configurations, and ablation procedures. No experimental setting is revised or added.

E4.justification: The component and loss ablations, interaction tests, patch-size and global-feature analyses, parameter comparisons, fusion-depth studies, and qualitative case studies are retained unchanged in Section 4.4 and Appendices A–B.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Main-text and appendix results retain the same point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 retain their numerical results, including MPG-SAM 2 J&F scores of 73.9 on Ref-YouTube-VOS, 72.4 on Ref-DAVIS17, and 53.7 on MeViS. Figures 4–5 also retain the same qualitative examples and findings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and their associated mathematical definitions remain unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about mask-prior prompting, global-historical aggregation, temporal consistency, and superior RVOS benchmark performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning global context, mask-guided features, redundant information from deeper fusion, and parameter efficiency are unchanged. The offline-RVOS scope and appendix case-study explanations are retained without new substantive limitations.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix A retain the same initialization, hyperparameters, hardware, memory settings, and Tiny-model configuration. The code-access statement and repository URL are also unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds three background references concerning video object segmentation, remote-sensing visual grounding, and customized SAM 2 for remote-sensing segmentation (references 21, 22, and 39). Existing references and the substantive novelty positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v5 expands the Wuhan University affiliation and adds funding acknowledgments after Appendix B. Apart from these additions and citation insertions, body prose, terminology, and section ordering remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 corrects the mask-decoder label and routes global unified features to pixel-level fusion and global video features to object-level fusion. Table 1 moves from page 6 to page 7, with surrounding layout reflow; all figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Figure 2's corrected decoder label and feature-routing arrows remove inconsistencies with the method text and Figure 3 already present in v3, modestly improving architectural clarity. Experiments, results, claims, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall quality gain is limited.
